subfield: Condensed matter physics: moiré quantum materials and strongly correlated electrons
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees collapses the electronic bandwidth, creating nearly flat bands where interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers realized this experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. This theory-experiment loop created an entirely new, tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological matter: a twist angle and a gate voltage now replace chemical synthesis. The field it launched has produced orbital magnetism, quantum anomalous Hall states, correlated Chern insulators, Wigner crystals, and, in related moiré systems, the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect. These phenomena have been confirmed by transport, local imaging and spectroscopy in many laboratories worldwide. Moiré engineering has changed how we discover and control emergent quantum phases, and it is a lasting contribution to physics.
